attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Patel, MD
Department: Neurology
Visit Type: icu

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home lasting 2 minutes with persistent fever

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 1-year-old male with history of septic arthritis and meningitis in 2020 presents with fever and seizure. The seizure lasted for 2 minutes and involved generalized tonic-clonic movements. The infant has had a fever of 38.9°C (102°F) for the past day, which has not improved with acetaminophen.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Septic arthritis of the knee (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Acute bacterial meningitis (diagnosed 2020-07-15)

He is up to date with his immunizations.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D3 drops 400 IU orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No known family history of immunodeficiency or primary autoimmune disorders
- Maternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Infant.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows: temperature 39°C (102.2°F), heart rate 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate 40 breaths per minute, and blood pressure 90/60 mmHg.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant appears lethargic and has a bulging fontanelle. The remainder of the physical examination is nonfocal.

LABORATORY DATA:
A complete blood count shows a white blood cell count of 15,000/µL with 70% neutrophils. A lumbar puncture is performed, and the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis reveals: - WBC: 300 cells/µL (80% neutrophils) - RBC: 20 cells/µL - Protein: 100 mg/dL - Glucose: 20 mg/dL (serum glucose 90 mg/dL)

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Elena Rodriguez, MD
Department: Orthopedics
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
2-day history of fever and irritability with crying when right leg is touched or moved, especially during diaper changes

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The parents report that the infant cries when his right leg is touched or moved, especially during diaper changes. They deny any recent trauma, cough, runny nose, or contact with sick individuals.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D3 drops 400 IU orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No known family history of immunodeficiency or primary autoimmune disorders
- Maternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Infant.

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 38.7°C (101.7°F), heart rate is 150 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 40 breaths per minute.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals a swollen right knee with warmth and limited range of motion due to pain. The rest of the examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies show:

- White blood cell count: 18,000/mm³ (Normal: 5,000-15,000/mm³)
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR): 60 mm/hr (Normal: 0-20 mm/hr)
- C-reactive protein (CRP): 4.5 mg/dL (Normal: <1.0 mg/dL)

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. James Park, MD
Department: Infectious Diseases
Visit Type: inpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
2-day history of fever and irritability with refusal to feed since this morning

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents six months after right knee septic arthritis. The mother reports that the child has been crying more than usual and has refused to feed since this morning.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Septic arthritis of the knee (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

He is up to date with his vaccinations.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D3 drops 400 IU orally daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No known family history of immunodeficiency or primary autoimmune disorders
- Maternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Infant.

VITAL SIGNS:
38.9°C (102°F)

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant is febrile, appears lethargic, and cries when being held. His anterior fontanelle is full and tense. A neurological examination reveals a high-pitched cry and neck stiffness.

LABORATORY DATA:
Initial laboratory tests reveal:

- White blood cell count: 15,000/mm³ with 80% neutrophils
- Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
- Platelet count: 250,000/mm³
- C-reactive protein: 40 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L)
- Blood culture: Pending
